version.changelog: Clarify only API key is required; no webhook secret in scope

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: pamela-call
Version: 1.1.7

The skill bundle is benign. It integrates with the 'Pamela' AI calling service, requiring a `PAMELA_API_KEY` as explicitly declared in `SKILL.md` metadata. The documentation provides standard installation instructions for SDKs and CLI usage examples, all pointing to the legitimate `thisispamela.com` domain. There is no evidence of prompt injection attempts, data exfiltration, malicious execution, or other harmful behaviors beyond the stated purpose of making API calls to the Pamela service.

llm.summary: The skill's requested permissions and runtime instructions are consistent with a third‑party outbound calling service: it only asks for a Pamela API key and the README describes SDK/CLI usage and webhooks for call lifecycle events.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the requested capability. The only declared requirement is PAMELA_API_KEY, which is appropriate for an outbound-calling API. Declared SDKs, CLI, webhooks, and billing details align with a telephony service.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md contains only usage/install instructions, example code, and webhook info for the Pamela service. It does not instruct the agent to read unrelated system files, harvest other environment variables, or exfiltrate data to third parties beyond the documented Pamela endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill (no install spec or code files). It recommends installing packages from npm/pypi by name, which is typical. Because the skill does not perform any automatic downloads or install steps itself, there is no arbitrary-code install risk in the skill bundle.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only one credential is required (PAMELA_API_KEY) and that directly maps to the declared primary credential for the described API. The examples show how the key is used; no unrelated secrets or multiple unrelated credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not always-enabled, requests no config paths, and does not ask to modify other skills or system-wide settings. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but is not in itself unusual for this service-integration skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent with a commercial outbound-call API, but treat the PAMELA_API_KEY as a sensitive secret: only provide a key you trust, monitor usage and billing, and prefer a scoped/test key if available. Verify the npm/pypi package authors and the domains (thisispamela.com, docs.thisispamela.com, api.thisispamela.com) before installing SDKs. If you will call or collect sensitive information (health, payment, personal data), confirm compliance requirements and enable webhook signature verification as documented. Finally, because the skill bundle is instruction-only and came from an unknown registry owner, you may want to confirm the vendor identity (website, docs, support contact) before entering live API keys or enabling autonomous agent use.
